inherited_rules.mutation_rule: This protocol operationalizes but does not modify either inherited frozen rule.

candidate_order.stop: Stop after eight behaviorally unique admitted candidates or after all thirteen inventoried attempts are accounted for.

candidate_bundle.candidate_identity: For a final worktree, use the exact acquired file hashes recorded in the source inventory. For a checkpoint, read the three files from the exact recorded commit/tree object.
candidate_bundle.allowed_literal_artifacts: Only a candidate-local literal artifact that static inspection proves is read while reconstructing or rendering level 1; record its path and SHA-256 before execution.
excluded: credentials, service URLs, and hidden state
candidate_bundle.no_reconstruction: Do not repair, rewrite, infer, or complete candidate code. Adapter code may normalize only the public fixed interface and must be byte-identical for every attempt.

runtime_isolation.filesystem: read-only candidate and P0 mounts, read-only root filesystem, isolated writable tmpfs only
runtime_isolation.process: unprivileged user, all Linux capabilities dropped, no-new-privileges, bounded memory, CPU, PID count, and timeout
runtime_isolation.secrets: No host credentials, environment secrets, released session token, or service URL may be mounted or copied.
runtime_isolation.dependencies: Build and hash one local runtime image before behavior execution. Candidate-time dependency installation and network access are forbidden.
runtime_isolation.candidate_runtime_calls: No ARC, LLM, hosted service, API, browser, external memory, or OIA call.

opened_prefix.replay_requirement: initial_state_reconstruction(1, P0) followed by state_renderer must reproduce the exact settled P0 frame; declared status is RUNNING at level 1 with zero levels completed.

finite_boundary.words: Lexicographic Cartesian order over ACTION1 through ACTION4 at lengths 1, then 2, then 3.
finite_boundary.reset: Every word begins in a fresh process reconstructed only from the immutable P0 input.
finite_boundary.frame_encoding: Uppercase hexadecimal raster rows joined by LF with one final LF; SHA-256 is computed over those bytes.
finite_boundary.trace_envelope: Canonical JSON UTF-8 with sorted object keys, compact separators, exact integers, and no NaN. Each step records final settled frame SHA-256, predicted status, modeled level/progress integer fields when present, and deterministic error category.
finite_boundary.intermediate_frames: Preserve candidate-emitted intermediate frames if any; absence is not a rejection and no animation-fidelity claim is made.

screening.static: Record source hashes, local imports, external dependencies, literal file reads, and forbidden-call scan without importing candidate code.
screening.p0: Reject a candidate whose isolated reconstruction/render does not exactly replay P0.
screening.provisional: For each remaining candidate, run all 84 words once with PYTHONHASHSEED=0. Record the complete trace signature. Retain the first candidate in frozen order for each distinct signature.
screening.promotion: For each provisionally unique candidate, run every word twice in fresh processes for PYTHONHASHSEED 0, 1, 5, and 10. All canonical traces for a word must be byte-identical.
screening.accounting: Record every admitted, duplicate, replay-failed, nondeterministic, dependency-blocked, timeout, and forbidden-runtime attempt.

success_condition: candidate_frontier_feasible requires at least two replay-consistent, deterministic, behaviorally non-equivalent candidates. Two is sufficient; three through eight is preferred.
stop_conditions: Any candidate process attempts network, service, credential, ARC, LLM/API, or non-allowlisted host-file access.
Runtime isolation cannot be demonstrated before candidate import.
The exact candidate or P0 hashes do not match the source inventory.
Eight behaviorally unique candidates are admitted or all attempts are accounted for.
claim_boundary: Opened Track A candidate admission and bounded behavioral deduplication only. No real ARC intervention, full ARC adapter, OIA separator synthesis, ontology-revision claim, global equivalence, planning or decision superiority, sealed evaluation, or Track B claim.
